analysis.title: AI's Moment Of Truth As Hyperscalers Take The Stand
key_insights: October's AI selloff is read as structural rather than forced selling like July's: investors question whether monetization and AI demand can keep pace with the size and cost of the infrastructure build, after a sharp repricing in funding costs.
Meta's lack of clarity on the path of AI capital intensity did little to ease concerns about the scale and returns of the infrastructure build, pushing risk and positioning to extremes.

Over three weeks, rising funding costs drove a 17% retracement in UBS's AI Winner basket. The funding-sensitive neocloud complex fell 34%, twice as much, while hyperscalers fell 7%, as investors rotated up the quality ladder within AI and shorts pressed low-quality names.

UBS's L/S Momentum Factor underperformed the L/S Quality Factor by about 24% over three weeks. Momentum's +66% peak outperformance versus quality has fully unwound. The AI Winner basket underperformed XLP by 24% over the same period.
SMH, SPY and QQQ are all at key support: SMH at the 200d MA (215), SPY at the 100d MA (758), QQQ at the 3-month low (700). UBS expects risk to pivot hard this week.

UBS PB data: through October, long exposure was cut from the 90th percentile to the 15th percentile (5Y) while shorts rose from the 15th to the 80th percentile. Net exposure is at the 25th percentile and gross is above the 90th percentile.
Hyperscaler earnings are a circuit breaker for the AI trade. The market will focus on the relationship between cloud growth and capex.

If Azure, AWS and Google Cloud stay strong, management keeps describing AI demand as capacity constrained and forward capex plans hold, the move would look like positioning, funding and return-on-spend concerns rather than a change in AI demand.
The more concerning outcome is slowing cloud growth alongside another leg higher in capex, which would validate the bear case that infrastructure spending is getting ahead of monetization.

For Nvidia, Micron and the AI infrastructure complex, this week turns on whether hyperscalers can show revenue arriving fast enough to justify the build. UBS says price action over the next seven days will likely dictate the next seven weeks.
The sharp rise in shorts leaves the market vulnerable to a squeeze, while breaks of technical supports would shift the market from rotation to broad-based selling.

FOMC: the market expects little from Fed Chair Warsh this week, with 2bp of a hike priced. UBS US Economics expects the message to be that more work is needed and the job is not done. UBS's title calls for a spike in October and hikes in December and January.
